sentences.text:
Shri Rahul Yadav, counsel for the respondents No.1 and 2.
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company under Section 173(1)
of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by order dated 18.07.2022 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nimar, District- Mandleshwar (MP) in MACC No./300105/2016 on the ground of false implication of the insured vehicle.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nimar, District- Mandleshwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (2) The brief facts of the case are that deceased Lakhan was on his way while driving the motorcycle bearing number MP10MA-1073, suddenly the driver of offending motorcycle bearing number MP10MP-5291 dashed the motorcycle of Lakhan, as a result of which he sustained injuries and died during the treatment on 20.07.2015.
(3) Claimant has filed the claim application before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
(4) The appellant and respondents No.3 and 4 have filed their written statements before the claims Tribunal.

(5) The Tribunal has framed the issues and after taking evidence of both the parties has passed the award dated 18.07.2022, holding that the said accident has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:24051 2 MA-4818-2022 caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle due to which Lakhan (deceased) has been died and has awarded Rs.4,58,000/- to the claimant with an interest of 6% per annum to be paid by appellant and respondent No.3 and 4 Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Ambu on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32431123/
1 jointly and severally.

sentences.text: (6) Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the ground that the FIR was lodged after eight days of the accident.
The accident took place on 12.07.2015 at about 5:30 pm and FIR was lodged on 20.07.2015 to secure the compensation from the Insurance Company.
Thereafter the offending vehicle was seized and the driver of the said vehicle was arrested by the police.

He further submits that FIR was lodged against some unknown vehicle and the eye-witness of the incident has not supported the case of claimants and he has stated in cross-examination that he reached the spot after the accident and he was hostile in the Magistrate Court.
During trial, the driver of offending vehicle was acquitted by the Magistrate Court.
On the above grounds, the appellant prays that this appeal be allowed and the Insurance Company be exonerated from the liability.
(7) Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
(8) On perusal of the record, it was found that the accident took place on 12.07.2015 at about 5:30 pm and during treatment he died on 20.07.2015.

According to MLC A/5 and A/6, it was found that the deceased was taken to the hospital for treatment and according to postmortem report mentioned in Page No.2 in which it was mentioned that the cause of death was road traffic accident.
(9) In FIR Ex.P/2 it was mentioned that due to busy in the treatment of deceased, delay has been caused in lodging the FIR.

In FIR Ex.P/2 it is true that the registration number of the offending vehicle was not mentioned but the name of driver of offending vehicle was mentioned and after due investigation, the police has filed the chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle.
(10) Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has submitted that FIR was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:24051 3 MA-4818-2022 delayed and the same was not properly explained.
(11) It is settled law that delay in filing the FIR is not fatal either in criminal case or in claim case provided that sufficient and cogent reason for delay in filing the FIR is given.
The Apex Court in the case of Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226 in Para 20 & 21

entities.text: Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held as under:-
[20] It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Ambu on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32431123/
2 implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Ambu on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [21] The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.

Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:24051 4 MA-4818-2022 lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

(12) It is true that the accident was occurred on 12.07.2015 and the information was sent to the police and Pre-MLC was also done on the same day in which it was also mentioned that the deceased was took to the hospital for the treatment in the road traffic accident and in the post-mortem report the death was caused due to the motorcycle accident.
In the present case, in the accident the member of the claimant family has died.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Therefore on the basis of delayed FIR, claim case cannot be dismissed.

(13) Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has submitted that eye witness Anandram has stated in cross-examination that accident has not occurred in his presence and he reached on the spot after the accident so he is not the eye witness in the present case.

The claim application has been filed under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act in which negligence of the driver of offending vehicle need not to be proved and the only thing needs to be proved is that accident occurred due to the use of offending vehicle.

(14) In the present case, Anandram (AW/2) has clearly stated in his evidence that accident occurred due to the use of offending vehicle and the police has also filed the chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle and the driver and owner of the offending vehicle had not dared to come to the witness box so they cannot rebutted the evidence or witness or criminal documents.

(15) Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has submitted that Tribunal on the basis of registration of FIR and its consequential proceedings has held that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:24051 5 MA-4818-2022 accident has been caused by the insured vehicle whereas all the eye-witness of final report Ex.P/1 has turned hostile in criminal case and has not supported Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Ambu on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32431123/
3

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Ambu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the prosecution case and JMFC has acquitted the driver Anandram from the said offence which is evident from Ex.D/1 and Ex.D/5.

(16) In the present case, the prosecution witness was substantially intact in his verdict as he was not the relative of the deceased so it cannot be expected from him to first come to the police-station and lodge the FIR and to give the information to the police for registration of the offending vehicle.

The Investigating Officer of the criminal case investigates the matter and thereafter he files the chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle who has not entered into the witness box before the claims Tribunal.
So he is unable to rebutt the evidence.

(17) In view of the aforesaid discussion and considering the evidence of claimant and criminal documents, in the considered opinion of this court, it was found that the claims Tribunal has elaborately discussed everything in the award that driver of offending vehicle is guilty and therefore the Tribunal has not committed any error in holding that the driver of offending vehicle has caused the accident.
Hence, the appellant has failed to prove that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the aforesaid offence for seeking compensation.
Accordingly this appeal is devoid of merit and is hereby dismissed.
(18) The appeal is dismissed accordingly.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE Arun/-
